as_told.title: NASA transient lunar phenomena archive centred on Aristarchus

plain: Lunar transient phenomena are short-lived flashes, glows, clouds or changes that people say they have seen on the surface of the Moon. A researcher named Randall Carlson, on Jesse Michels's podcast, says there are hundreds of recorded examples. According to him, they include the Moon giving off gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapor. A different guest on a later episode tells it another way. That guest says NASA, the US space agency, keeps a catalogue of these events going back hundreds of years, gathered from amateur and professional astronomers on Earth. In that telling, many of the reports center on a crater called Aristarchus. The tellers raise it because, if true, it would mean the Moon is far more active, and stranger, than most people assume.
